# Distillation facts (public, our setup)
Task: causal per-row regression on market streams (211 inputs/row; 2 targets t0,t1; metric = pooled weighted Pearson, weights |clip(y,2)|, rows>=99). Model: Linear+GELU encoder -> 2-layer GRU 256 (or 384) -> head [GRU;skip] -> 2 outputs + aux. Fold 1 validation, one-run noise sd ~0.002, seed sd ~0.001.
Teachers (3 epochs scratch): plain h256 ~0.6660; muon-all h384 mean 0.670 (5 seeds .6702/.6715/.6703/.6695/.6679); prop0 ~0.6678.
Student pipeline today: warm-start from a parent checkpoint (0.666 class), 3 epochs AdamW lr 1e-4, loss = 0.7 * MSE(student, mean teacher cached outputs) + 0.3 * label loss (weighted), teachers are 2 seeds' cached predictions on train split. Results: student from 2 h256 teachers 0.66938; from 2 h384 teachers 0.66836; NO teacher continuation (same schedule) 0.66861 => teacher signal worth only +0.0008.
Diverse pair blends (h256+h384 members) give +0.003 over a single; seeds of the same recipe give ~+0.001; members share 96-99.9% of residual.
Residual EDA: error concentrated in market class 3 (50% weight, 69% residual SS, local corr .44 vs .75-.81); 94% of residual is per-run level offset between label runs (labels step only at book events); label leads features ~1 row; t0/t1 difference mode under-dispersed.
Serving constraint: final model must run CPU int8 within ~13 portal-min per model (GRU 256 ok; 384 ~2x cost). Training-time compute is relaxed. Teachers may be much larger / ensembles; student must be small.
Queued/untested: out-of-sample path distillation (augmented random paths fed to teachers, student trained on teacher outputs); multi-teacher; hidden-state matching.
Not available: any external data or pretrained weights beyond supplied data.

Data: `datasets/train.parquet` (about 10.6k sequences), `datasets/valid.parquet` (1,873 sequences, 4 component-disjoint folds, fold 1 = 457 evaluation sequences in 149 components (older notes say 468)). 2 order books + 8 extra] --> B[event features
99 per row] 19: A --> C[raw 112] 20: B --> D[concat: 211 inputs] 21: C --> D 22: D --> E[z-score with fit-set mean/std
folded into the first layer at export] 23: E --> F[Linear 211 to 256 + GELU] 24: F --> G[2-layer GRU, h=256, zero initial state] 25: G --> H[head: concat GRU out + encoder skip
Linear 512 to 256, GELU, Linear 256 to 2] 26: H --> I[t0, t1 prediction per row] 27: ``` 28: 29: ### Event features (99 per row; [`src/wnn/features.py`](../../../../../src/wnn/features.py)) 30: First differences of the instrument-0 price block, instrument-0 volume block and instrument-1 price block (22 + 22 + 22), eight event flags (price move, bid/ask volume change, trade price/volume, instrument-1 price/volume/trade), three "rows since last event" counters, and the last non-zero price difference (22). They are computed causally inside the trainer (`event_features_torch`) and by the native engine at serving. Inputs total 112 + 99 = **211** (the `normalization_identity` shape in every `history.json`). 31: 32: ## 2. Architecture (and the attention question) 33: 34: * **No attention in the best model.** Source: [`RNNModel` in `src/wnn/nn.py`](../../../../../research/campaign_2026-10-06/bandit_continuation/continuous_execution_E529/h230_source_v6_lead/src/wnn/nn.py) with `enc=linear`. Input normalisation uses a fit-set mean/std buffer; at export the normalisation is folded into this layer so zero raw inputs can be skipped column by column. 36: * **Recurrent core:** PyTorch `nn.GRU(256, 256, num_layers=2, batch_first=True)` (cuDNN fused). **State:** the initial hidden state is zero (`h=None`); it is reset at the start of every sequence; during training a sequence is processed in chunks of 1000-2000 rows with the state carried from chunk to chunk and **detached** (truncated BPTT), so gradients reach back one chunk only. plus auxiliary structure (0.3) and next-change (0.3) heads | 50: | Row weighting | `--propensity`, `--valid-true-mask`: the official scored mask is only known for valid sequences, so training rows are weighted by an estimated probability of being scored (power 2, floor 0.03) and valid sequences use the true mask | 51: | Time | about 560-620 s per epoch on the local GPU, about 45 min for 3 epochs | 52: 53: ![learning rate](plots/lr_schedules.png) 54: 55: **What the logs and checkpoints keep.** Every run directory in `artifacts/runs//` (9.3 GB total) holds `model_ep{E}.pt` per epoch, `model.pt`, `training_state.pt`, `history.json` (per-epoch seconds, optimizer attempts/skipped steps, sample-order and normalisation hashes) and `provenance.json` (source and split hashes). **Validation is deliberately not computed during fitting** (`--no-eval-during-fit`: campaign rule), so `history.json` says `evaluation: withheld`; coef 0.15 each] 68: T2[full_finetuned: since-weight finetunes
coef 0.10 each] 69: T3[raw_wmse: since s3, s4
coef 0.125 each] 70: T4[samefold baseline: two width-384 raw-wmse runs
coef 0.03125 each] 71: end 72: T --> CACHE[(distillation cache: per-row predictions of every family
cache/h230_four_family_fold1_source_20261009_r1
sum of coefficients 0.8125)] 73: CACHE --> BLEND[target = 0.3 x true label + 0.7 x blended teacher] 74: P[parent: c20261003_combo_s3_f1 epoch 3
warm start of the student] --> S 75: BLEND --> S[student: same 2x256 GRU
AdamW lr 1e-4, one-cycle, 3 epochs, batch 16
+ family head weight 0.1] 76: S --> OUT[served: first 2 outputs] 77: ``` 78: 79: * Recipe (launch file: [`done/72_h230-f1-s3-ep3-chunk1000-fit-r1.json`](../local_queue_r1/done/72_h230-f1-s3-ep3-chunk1000-fit-r1.json); the best student `h230_f1_s3_ep3` uses chunk 2000): `--init c20261003_combo_s3_f1@ep3`, `--distill-alpha 0.7`, `--distill-family-head --distill-family-weight 0.1 --distill-family-target-mode raw`, `--optim adamw --lr 1e-4 --sched onecycle --epochs 3 --batch 16`, no bootstrap substitution (`--distill-boot-h 0`). 80: * Why it works at all: the student is a *warm-started* copy of a good scratch teacher, then pulled toward the average of several differently trained teachers (their errors are only partly shared: pairwise correlation 0.95-0.99). A fold-k run trains on `train` plus the valid sequences of the other folds and evaluates on fold k only ([`splits/fold1.json`](../../../../../research/campaign_2026-09-29/artifacts/splits/fold1.json)). Fold levels differ: about 0.668 / 0.679 / 0.703 / 0.707. 86: * **Noise (measured, [`hpo/VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md`](../../../../../hpo/VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md)):** seed-to-seed sd 0.0010; evaluation-unit noise of a paired difference sd 0.0018; one-run one-fold A/B comparison sd about 0.0022 (95% ±0.0043). Pruning compares after fold 1. Folds 2 and 3 are **never** used for search; `orchestrator confirm` runs the top finalists once on them (pre-registered rule: confirm if mean delta ≥ 0 and class-3 delta ≥ 0). 94: * **State today (56 asked, 50 told: 18 complete, 28 pruned, 4 failed):** best by objective: trial 35 (0.66876: muon_hidden, lr 1e-3, WSD-linear, h384, dropout 0.16, SWA), 27 (0.66779, 3 layers, wmse_gcorr, class-3 weight 2.45), 46, 41, 13. T2: trial 2 (h384) 0.70737 on fold 3; trial 27 0.70249 on fold 2. 95: 96: ![HPO](plots/hpo_fold_scatter.png) 97: 98: ### The "delta +0.002" evidence ([`hpo/evidence/scratch_effects_fold1.json`](../../../../../hpo/evidence/scratch_effects_fold1.json), [`scripts/evidence_report.py`](../../../../../scripts/evidence_report.py)) 99: It compares 47 scratch models on fold 1 against the mean of four default-recipe runs (0.66642, seed sd 0.00106). The largest raw deltas are +0.0028 (h384 with dropout 0.2), +0.0022 (gated), +0.0017 (h384 fixed-mix), +0.0016 (h384). **All 95% intervals cover zero** (about ±0.005: component bootstrap and seed noise in quadrature), and after empirical-Bayes shrinkage (true-effect sd 0.0015 vs measurement sd 0.0024) they are +0.0003..+0.0006. They are therefore *hypotheses*, not findings. 100: 101: ![forest](plots/evidence_forest.png) 102: 103: How we use it: (1) it set the decision thresholds and narrowed the HPO space (epochs ≤ 5, no corr/Huber/TCN, width ≤ 384); (2) the consistent sign of width 384 across **four** folds (mean +0.0012) is the only lever that survived; (3) the high-raw-delta variants (h384+dropout, gated) are the candidates worth a confirmation on reserved folds 2/3 and a place in a *diverse* ensemble, not a ranking claim; (4) it fixes how many runs a claim needs (about 4 folds × 3 seeds per arm for ±0.002). 104: 105: ## 7. Local validation: which result is the best example 106: 107: Fold 1 (457 evaluation sequences, 149 components; bootstrap over components, 1000 draws; paired intervals against the matched control `r3_ctrl_f1_s3_e3`, produced by [`make_solution_report.py`](../../../../../scripts/make_solution_report.py), table in [`fold1_ci.json`](fold1_ci.json)): 108: 109: | Model | Fold-1 WP | 95% CI (unpaired) | Δ vs control s3 | 95% CI of Δ (paired) | 110: |---|---|---|---|---| 111: | student: distilled from h256 scratch teachers (`vt_f1_dsq_t256`) | 0.66938 | [0.6229, 0.7127] | +0.0033 | [+0.0011, +0.0059] | 112: | **student: H230 ep3, four teacher families (`h230_f1_s3_ep3`)** | **0.66922** | [0.6220, 0.7125] | **+0.0032** | **[+0.0016, +0.0049]** | 113: | teacher: scratch h384 chunk500 3 ep | 0.66900 | [0.6217, 0.7113] | +0.0029 | [+0.0004, +0.0057] | 114: | student ep3 + bootstrap 8 | 0.66821 | [0.6215, 0.7119] | +0.0022 | [+0.0004, +0.0041] | 115: | teacher: scratch default (v6 trainer) s3 / s4 | 0.66606 / 0.66582 | | 0 / -0.0002 | [-0.0022, +0.0015] | 116: 117: ![fold 1 CI](plots/fold1_ci.png) 118: 119: **Best example to explain: `h230_f1_s3_ep3`** (fold-1 WP 0.66922). It is the only model whose paired improvement over the control is large relative to its interval (+0.0032, lower bound +0.0016) and it has the cleanest provenance (one declared parent, four independently trained teacher families, fixed coefficients). The unpaired intervals (±0.045) are wide because sequences differ hugely in difficulty; paired differences are what matter. Caveats: this is one seed and one fold, the paired interval measures evaluation-unit variation only (add training-seed sd 0.001), the fold is exposed after many selections, and the public score of the corresponding fold-1-held-out student family was 0.6639 (P2) - local differences of +0.003 have not reliably transferred. 120: 121: ## 8. Serving 122: 123: Native Rust engine ([`native/src/rnn_fast.rs`](../../../../../native/src/rnn_fast.rs), int16 weight panels, AVX2, normalisation folded into the first layer, event features computed in the engine, state reset per sequence, deterministic). About 74 µs/row for width 256 on one core; about 33-37 min for the 39M-row test when run alone on the portal. A package is accepted only after Python 3.11 offline checks, ABI, reset/determinism and prediction agreement (corr ≥ 0.99998 with the GPU model). 124: 125: ## 9. Why the ceiling is where it is (new this session) 126: 127: ![ladder](plots/lookahead_ladder.png) 128: 129: With the same GRU and *future* rows visible the score is 0.666 (causal), 0.680 (2 rows ahead), 0.711 (8), 0.780 (32), 0.891 (128), 0.960 (512). The label is a smooth function of a long future path, so the causal model is a price-move **forecaster**; recipe knobs (chunk length, bootstrap, snapping columns, width, epochs) all moved the score by ≤ ±0.001-0.002. See [LOOP_LOG pass 33-38](../LOOP_LOG_20261010.md) and [SANTANDER_LESSONS_AND_SERVING_SPEED](../SANTANDER_LESSONS_AND_SERVING_SPEED_20261010.md). 130: 131: ## 10. Where to read next 132: * Current state and decisions: [`specs/current-state.md`](../../../../../specs/current-state.md), [`LOOP_LOG_20261010.md`](../LOOP_LOG_20261010.md), [`CONTRACT_R3_TEACHER_CEILING_20261010.md`](../CONTRACT_R3_TEACHER_CEILING_20261010.md). 133: * Hypotheses H-321..H-339: [`research/hypotheses.jsonl`](../../../../../research/hypotheses.jsonl). 134: * Ideator outputs: [`external_ideation_20261010/`](../external_ideation_20261010/) (SYNTHESIS, round 2 and 3, BNP and own-notes mining). display.text:
# Current best local solution, explained (2026-10-10) Scope: what the best local-validation model is, how the data become predictions, how it is trained and distilled, what HPO does, and what the numbers do and do not support. Everything cited is a file in this repository; plots are generated by [`scripts/make_solution_report.py`](../../../../../scripts/make_solution_report.py) and [`scripts/extract_train_loss.py`](../../../../../scripts/extract_train_loss.py) from saved predictions, logs and ledgers (nothing is redrawn by hand). **One-sentence summary.** A 2-layer GRU (width 256, no attention) over 211 per-row inputs is first trained from scratch as a *teacher* (Muon on the recurrent matrices, one-cycle schedule, weighted-MSE on the official metric weights), then a *student* with the same architecture is warm-started from a teacher and fine-tuned for 3 epochs on a blend of the true labels (30%) and the averaged predictions of four teacher families (70%). The student is what is served (one core, about 74 µs/row in the native int16 kernel). --- ## 1. Data and what the 112 columns are * Each sequence is 20,000 rows × 112 anonymous float columns; two targets (t0, t1) per row; the metric is scored only on rows ≥ 99 and where the official mask is true. Data: `datasets/train.parquet` (about 10.6k sequences), `datasets/valid.parquet` (1,873 sequences, 4 component-disjoint folds, fold 1 = 457 evaluation sequences in 149 components (older notes say 468)). Sequences are consecutive 20k-row chunks of 3,288 continuous streams ([findings](../../../../../research/findings-2026-09-26.md)). * The column layout is an **order book of two instruments** ([`src/wnn/data.py`](../../../../../src/wnn/data.py)): per instrument 11 bid prices, 11 ask prices, 11 bid volumes, 11 ask volumes, 4 trade prices, 4 trade volumes (52 columns; instruments at offsets 0 and 52) plus 8 extra columns (104-111). Prices and volumes are quantile-transformed; many columns are held constant between updates (multi-rate clocks: blocks update on 12%, 15%, 31%, 40%, 70% or 100% of rows). * Targets are trade PnLs against a common future price F: `t0 = F - ask`, `t1 = bid - F`; the label is piecewise constant in time (mean run 9.5 rows) and defined by the **future** book. A teacher that may see future rows scores far higher (section 9). * Metric `global_wp_clip2_v1` ([`src/wnn/gmetric.py`](../../../../../src/wnn/gmetric.py)): Pearson pooled over rows and both targets with weights |clip(y, 2)|, both prediction and target clipped to ±2. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[20,000 x 112 raw columns
2 order books + 8 extra] --> B[event features
99 per row] A --> C[raw 112] B --> D[concat: 211 inputs] C --> D D --> E[z-score with fit-set mean/std
folded into the first layer at export] E --> F[Linear 211 to 256 + GELU] F --> G[2-layer GRU, h=256, zero initial state] G --> H[head: concat GRU out + encoder skip
Linear 512 to 256, GELU, Linear 256 to 2] H --> I[t0, t1 prediction per row] ``` ### Event features (99 per row; [`src/wnn/features.py`](../../../../../src/wnn/features.py)) First differences of the instrument-0 price block, instrument-0 volume block and instrument-1 price block (22 + 22 + 22), eight event flags (price move, bid/ask volume change, trade price/volume, instrument-1 price/volume/trade), three "rows since last event" counters, and the last non-zero price difference (22). They are computed causally inside the trainer (`event_features_torch`) and by the native engine at serving. Inputs total 112 + 99 = **211** (the `normalization_identity` shape in every `history.json`). ## 2. Architecture (and the attention question) * **No attention in the best model.** Source: [`RNNModel` in `src/wnn/nn.py`](../../../../../research/campaign_2026-10-06/bandit_continuation/continuous_execution_E529/h230_source_v6_lead/src/wnn/nn.py) with `enc=linear`. A token-attention encoder (`enc=tokens`, PyTorch `nn.TransformerEncoderLayer`, per-block tokens with a CLS token) and a causal conv encoder exist as research options; they are not in the served model (the native engine supports the linear encoder only) and did not help. * **Encoder:** `Linear(211 -> 256)` then GELU (`z`). Input normalisation uses a fit-set mean/std buffer; at export the normalisation is folded into this layer so zero raw inputs can be skipped column by column. * **Recurrent core:** PyTorch `nn.GRU(256, 256, num_layers=2, batch_first=True)` (cuDNN fused). **State:** the initial hidden state is zero (`h=None`); it is reset at the start of every sequence; during training a sequence is processed in chunks of 1000-2000 rows with the state carried from chunk to chunk and **detached** (truncated BPTT), so gradients reach back one chunk only. At serving the native engine carries the state row by row and resets it at the sequence boundary. * **Head:** `[GRU output ; encoder output z] -> Linear(512,256) -> GELU -> Linear(256, n_out)`. `n_out` is 2 plus training-only auxiliary columns (structure head, next-change head, and for students a four-family head); only the first two outputs are served. * **Size:** about 1.04 M parameters at width 256 (log line `params 1.04M`). Width 384 is about 2.2× the cost per row and is not servable on the current kernel (733 µs/row vs 74 µs/row). ## 3. Teacher training (from scratch) Recipe of the default "scratch teacher" (`DEFAULTS` in [`hpo/space.py`](../../../../../hpo/space.py), a launched command in [`local_queue_r1/done/66_f0ep3s5-fit.json`](../local_queue_r1/done/66_f0ep3s5-fit.json)): | Item | Value | |---|---| | Optimizer | **Muon on the GRU weight matrices** (`weight_ih`, `weight_hh`; Newton-Schulz orthogonalisation, 5 steps, bf16; scope `rnn`) and **AdamW** for the input layer, head and biases (`MuonAdamW` in `src/wnn/optim.py`); lr 1e-3, weight decay 0.01, Muon lr multiplier 1 | | Schedule | OneCycle, 5% warm-up to the max lr, cosine decay to max_lr/(25·100) ([plot](plots/lr_schedules.png)); 3-4 epochs | | Batch | 32 sequences per step, chunk 1000 rows (20 optimizer steps per sequence), 373 batches and 7,460 optimizer steps per epoch (11,949 sampled sequences), fp16 autocast with GradScaler (about 5 skipped updates per epoch) | | Loss | weighted MSE on `y` clipped to ±2 with weights |clip(y,2)| (`--loss wmse`, chunk-normalised), the same weights as the metric; plus auxiliary structure (0.3) and next-change (0.3) heads | | Row weighting | `--propensity`, `--valid-true-mask`: the official scored mask is only known for valid sequences, so training rows are weighted by an estimated probability of being scored (power 2, floor 0.03) and valid sequences use the true mask | | Time | about 560-620 s per epoch on the local GPU, about 45 min for 3 epochs | ![learning rate](plots/lr_schedules.png) **What the logs and checkpoints keep.** Every run directory in `artifacts/runs//` (9.3 GB total) holds `model_ep{E}.pt` per epoch, `model.pt`, `training_state.pt`, `history.json` (per-epoch seconds, optimizer attempts/skipped steps, sample-order and normalisation hashes) and `provenance.json` (source and split hashes). **Validation is deliberately not computed during fitting** (`--no-eval-during-fit`: campaign rule), so `history.json` says `evaluation: withheld`; the learning curve is rebuilt afterwards from saved snapshots with [`scripts/snapshot_curve.py`](../../../../../scripts/snapshot_curve.py) ([plot](plots/learning_curves.png)). Training loss lives only in the text logs (`runtime/logs/*.log`, one line per 20 batches); until now it was not structured, so [`scripts/extract_train_loss.py`](../../../../../scripts/extract_train_loss.py) now parses it to CSV ([`train_loss_csv/`](train_loss_csv/), [plot](plots/train_loss.png)). Gap I recommend closing: persist the train loss in `history.json` per epoch. ![learning curves](plots/learning_curves.png) ![train loss](plots/train_loss.png) Reading the curves: on fold 1 the default run reaches 0.666 by epoch 2-3; the 6-epoch run peaks at 0.6671 at the end of epoch 3 and then drops (0.662, 0.649), i.e. memorisation, not under-training. Mid-epoch snapshots are as good as epoch ends. ## 4. Student and distillation (the top local model) ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph T[Four teacher families on the same fold, all independently trained] T1[strong: combo scratch s3, s4
coef 0.15 each] T2[full_finetuned: since-weight finetunes
coef 0.10 each] T3[raw_wmse: since s3, s4
coef 0.125 each] T4[samefold baseline: two width-384 raw-wmse runs
coef 0.03125 each] end T --> CACHE[(distillation cache: per-row predictions of every family
cache/h230_four_family_fold1_source_20261009_r1
sum of coefficients 0.8125)] CACHE --> BLEND[target = 0.3 x true label + 0.7 x blended teacher] P[parent: c20261003_combo_s3_f1 epoch 3
warm start of the student] --> S BLEND --> S[student: same 2x256 GRU
AdamW lr 1e-4, one-cycle, 3 epochs, batch 16
+ family head weight 0.1] S --> OUT[served: first 2 outputs] ``` * Recipe (launch file: [`done/72_h230-f1-s3-ep3-chunk1000-fit-r1.json`](../local_queue_r1/done/72_h230-f1-s3-ep3-chunk1000-fit-r1.json); the best student `h230_f1_s3_ep3` uses chunk 2000): `--init c20261003_combo_s3_f1@ep3`, `--distill-alpha 0.7`, `--distill-family-head --distill-family-weight 0.1 --distill-family-target-mode raw`, `--optim adamw --lr 1e-4 --sched onecycle --epochs 3 --batch 16`, no bootstrap substitution (`--distill-boot-h 0`). * Why it works at all: the student is a *warm-started* copy of a good scratch teacher, then pulled toward the average of several differently trained teachers (their errors are only partly shared: pairwise correlation 0.95-0.99). It gains about +0.003 over a scratch teacher; the gain comes from the chain (parent + blended targets), not from the student knob settings (twelve variants span 0.0010, see [LOOP_LOG](../LOOP_LOG_20261010.md), student-stage evidence entry). Distilling wider (384) or ensemble teachers into the 256 student did **not** transfer. * Files: cache builder [`scripts/build_distill_cache.py`](../../../../../scripts/build_distill_cache.py), pipeline [`scripts/distill_pipeline.py`](../../../../../scripts/distill_pipeline.py), cache metadata [`metadata.json`](../../../../../cache/h230_four_family_fold1_source_20261009_r1/metadata.json). ## 5. Validation: how scores are produced and how far to trust them * **Folds:** 4 component-disjoint folds of the 1,873 valid sequences (a component = a chain of consecutive chunks of one stream, so no neighbour leaks). A fold-k run trains on `train` plus the valid sequences of the other folds and evaluates on fold k only ([`splits/fold1.json`](../../../../../research/campaign_2026-09-29/artifacts/splits/fold1.json)). Fold levels differ: about 0.668 / 0.679 / 0.703 / 0.707. * **Noise (measured, [`hpo/VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md`](../../../../../hpo/VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md)):** seed-to-seed sd 0.0010; evaluation-unit noise of a paired difference sd 0.0018; one-run one-fold A/B comparison sd about 0.0022 (95% ±0.0043). Hardware drift about 0.0002. * **Tiers:** T0 screen (fold 1, 1 run: kills disasters only), T1 dev (folds 1 and 0, fold-difficulty adjusted), T2 confirm (folds 2 and 3 reserved, one evaluation per finalist), T3 train-holdout veto, T4 public (lineage level only). ## 6. HPO: what it is, what it tunes, how it is validated * **Yes, hyper-parameter optimisation:** Optuna TPE with durable SQLite + event log ([`hpo/studies/teacher_v2/`](../../../../../hpo/studies/teacher_v2/), code in [`hpo/`](../../../../../hpo/)), a MedianPruner, ask/tell over Vast lane B, a duplicate-proposal guard and per-tick seeding. * **Parameters (space v2, [`hpo/space.py`](../../../../../hpo/space.py)):** optimizer (`muon_rnn` / `muon_hidden`), lr 6e-4..2e-3, Muon multiplier 0.5..2, weight decay 3e-3..6e-2, schedule (`onecycle`, `wsd_sqrt`, `wsd_linear`, `sgdr`) with its conditional knobs, epochs {2,3,4,5}, width {256,320,384}, layers {2,3}, RNN init (`default`, `chrono`, `orth`, `chrono_orth`), loss (`wmse`, `wmse_gcorr`, `mix`), class-3 weight 0.7..2.5, weight averaging (none/EMA/SWA), dropout 0..0.25. Seeds are never searched. * **Validation inside HPO:** each trial runs on dev fold 1, then fold 0; the objective is the mean of the two with fold 0 reduced by the fold-difficulty offset (prior 0.0131, re-estimated from trials that have both). Pruning compares after fold 1. Folds 2 and 3 are **never** used for search; `orchestrator confirm` runs the top finalists once on them (pre-registered rule: confirm if mean delta ≥ 0 and class-3 delta ≥ 0). * **State today (56 asked, 50 told: 18 complete, 28 pruned, 4 failed):** best by objective: trial 35 (0.66876: muon_hidden, lr 1e-3, WSD-linear, h384, dropout 0.16, SWA), 27 (0.66779, 3 layers, wmse_gcorr, class-3 weight 2.45), 46, 41, 13. T2: trial 2 (h384) 0.70737 on fold 3; trial 27 0.70249 on fold 2. ![HPO](plots/hpo_fold_scatter.png) ### The "delta +0.002" evidence ([`hpo/evidence/scratch_effects_fold1.json`](../../../../../hpo/evidence/scratch_effects_fold1.json), [`scripts/evidence_report.py`](../../../../../scripts/evidence_report.py)) It compares 47 scratch models on fold 1 against the mean of four default-recipe runs (0.66642, seed sd 0.00106). The largest raw deltas are +0.0028 (h384 with dropout 0.2), +0.0022 (gated), +0.0017 (h384 fixed-mix), +0.0016 (h384). **All 95% intervals cover zero** (about ±0.005: component bootstrap and seed noise in quadrature), and after empirical-Bayes shrinkage (true-effect sd 0.0015 vs measurement sd 0.0024) they are +0.0003..+0.0006. They are therefore *hypotheses*, not findings. ![forest](plots/evidence_forest.png) How we use it: (1) it set the decision thresholds and narrowed the HPO space (epochs ≤ 5, no corr/Huber/TCN, width ≤ 384); (2) the consistent sign of width 384 across **four** folds (mean +0.0012) is the only lever that survived; (3) the high-raw-delta variants (h384+dropout, gated) are the candidates worth a confirmation on reserved folds 2/3 and a place in a *diverse* ensemble, not a ranking claim; (4) it fixes how many runs a claim needs (about 4 folds × 3 seeds per arm for ±0.002). ## 7. Local validation: which result is the best example Fold 1 (457 evaluation sequences, 149 components; bootstrap over components, 1000 draws; paired intervals against the matched control `r3_ctrl_f1_s3_e3`, produced by [`make_solution_report.py`](../../../../../scripts/make_solution_report.py), table in [`fold1_ci.json`](fold1_ci.json)): | Model | Fold-1 WP | 95% CI (unpaired) | Δ vs control s3 | 95% CI of Δ (paired) | |---|---|---|---|---| | student: distilled from h256 scratch teachers (`vt_f1_dsq_t256`) | 0.66938 | [0.6229, 0.7127] | +0.0033 | [+0.0011, +0.0059] | | **student: H230 ep3, four teacher families (`h230_f1_s3_ep3`)** | **0.66922** | [0.6220, 0.7125] | **+0.0032** | **[+0.0016, +0.0049]** | | teacher: scratch h384 chunk500 3 ep | 0.66900 | [0.6217, 0.7113] | +0.0029 | [+0.0004, +0.0057] | | student ep3 + bootstrap 8 | 0.66821 | [0.6215, 0.7119] | +0.0022 | [+0.0004, +0.0041] | | teacher: scratch default (v6 trainer) s3 / s4 | 0.66606 / 0.66582 | | 0 / -0.0002 | [-0.0022, +0.0015] | ![fold 1 CI](plots/fold1_ci.png) **Best example to explain: `h230_f1_s3_ep3`** (fold-1 WP 0.66922). It is the only model whose paired improvement over the control is large relative to its interval (+0.0032, lower bound +0.0016) and it has the cleanest provenance (one declared parent, four independently trained teacher families, fixed coefficients). The unpaired intervals (±0.045) are wide because sequences differ hugely in difficulty; paired differences are what matter. Caveats: this is one seed and one fold, the paired interval measures evaluation-unit variation only (add training-seed sd 0.001), the fold is exposed after many selections, and the public score of the corresponding fold-1-held-out student family was 0.6639 (P2) - local differences of +0.003 have not reliably transferred. ## 8. Serving Native Rust engine ([`native/src/rnn_fast.rs`](../../../../../native/src/rnn_fast.rs), int16 weight panels, AVX2, normalisation folded into the first layer, event features computed in the engine, state reset per sequence, deterministic). About 74 µs/row for width 256 on one core; about 33-37 min for the 39M-row test when run alone on the portal. A package is accepted only after Python 3.11 offline checks, ABI, reset/determinism and prediction agreement (corr ≥ 0.99998 with the GPU model). ## 9. Why the ceiling is where it is (new this session) ![ladder](plots/lookahead_ladder.png) With the same GRU and *future* rows visible the score is 0.666 (causal), 0.680 (2 rows ahead), 0.711 (8), 0.780 (32), 0.891 (128), 0.960 (512). The label is a smooth function of a long future path, so the causal model is a price-move **forecaster**; recipe knobs (chunk length, bootstrap, snapping columns, width, epochs) all moved the score by ≤ ±0.001-0.002. See [LOOP_LOG pass 33-38](../LOOP_LOG_20261010.md) and [SANTANDER_LESSONS_AND_SERVING_SPEED](../SANTANDER_LESSONS_AND_SERVING_SPEED_20261010.md). ## 10. Where to read next * Current state and decisions: [`specs/current-state.md`](../../../../../specs/current-state.md), [`LOOP_LOG_20261010.md`](../LOOP_LOG_20261010.md), [`CONTRACT_R3_TEACHER_CEILING_20261010.md`](../CONTRACT_R3_TEACHER_CEILING_20261010.md). * Hypotheses H-321..H-339: [`research/hypotheses.jsonl`](../../../../../research/hypotheses.jsonl). * Ideator outputs: [`external_ideation_20261010/`](../external_ideation_20261010/) (SYNTHESIS, round 2 and 3, BNP and own-notes mining).

part.text:
Here are 6 distinct distillation methods, each targeting a different failure mode in the current setup:

---

## 1. Longer Low-LR Output Distillation (Schedule Fix)

**Mechanism:** The current 3 epochs at lr 1e-4 is too short to fully adapt the warm-started student to the teacher ensemble. The student is already at 0.666-class, so it needs more time at a lower LR to converge to the ensemble mean.

**Why it fits:** The student is warm-started from a parent of the same class as the teachers. It's already close to the teacher mean, but 3 epochs at 1e-4 doesn't fully close the gap. The ensemble blend (+0.003) is better than any single teacher, but the student hasn't had time to match it.

**Loss/targets/schedule:** Same loss (0.7 * MSE(student, mean_teacher) + 0.3 * label), but 8-10 epochs at lr 3e-5 with cosine decay and 10% warmup. Batch 16, same architecture.

**Signal:** Mean teacher outputs (per-row).

**Data:** Train split.

**Cheapest falsifier:** Run 3 vs 6 vs 10 epochs on fold 1, compare to teacher ensemble blend. If 10 epochs ≈ 3 epochs, the bottleneck is capacity, not optimization.

**Expected gain:** +0.001-0.002.

**Literature:** Hinton et al. 2015, "Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network."

---

## 2. Per-Run Level-Offset Distillation

**Mechanism:** Distill the per-run mean prediction of the teacher ensemble, not per-row predictions. Aggregate both student and teacher predictions over each run (segment between label steps) and match the means.

**Why it fits:** 94% of residual is per-run level offset. The labels step at book events (mean run 9.5 rows). The student's dominant error is predicting the wrong level for a run. By distilling per-run means, we directly target this error source.

**Loss/targets/schedule:** Loss = 0.5 * MSE(student_run_mean, teacher_run_mean) + 0.3 * MSE(student, label) + 0.2 * MSE(student, teacher_per_row). 6 epochs, lr 5e-5, cosine. Run boundaries computed from label steps in the training data.

**Signal:** Per-run aggregated teacher predictions (mean over each run).

**Data:** Train split, grouped by run boundaries (from label step detection).

**Cheapest falsifier:** Compare per-run mean predictions between student and teacher ensemble on validation. If they match but per-row doesn't, the issue is within-run variation, not level.

**Expected gain:** +0.001-0.002.

**Literature:** Kim & Rush 2016, "Sequence-Level Knowledge Distillation."

---

## 3. Teacher Disagreement-Weighted Distillation

**Mechanism:** Weight the distillation loss by teacher ensemble variance. Where teachers agree, the target is reliable (upweight). Where they disagree, the target is uncertain (downweight or use as a hard example).

**Why it fits:** Class 3 has 50% weight and 69% residual SS. Teacher disagreement is highest exactly where the model is wrong. By weighting the loss, we focus learning on the reliable signal and avoid fitting noise.

**Loss/targets/schedule:** Loss = MSE(student, mean_teacher) * (1 + alpha * teacher_variance_normalized). Alpha = 1.0. 6 epochs, lr 5e-5, cosine. Teacher variance computed across the 2-4 teacher predictions per row.

**Signal:** Teacher ensemble variance (per-row, per-target).

**Data:** Train split.

**Cheapest falsifier:** Correlate teacher variance with student error on validation. If high-variance rows have high student error, the weighting is working.

**Expected gain:** +0.001-0.003.

**Literature:** Lakshminarayanan et al. 2017, "Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles."

---

## 4. Hidden State Distillation (FitNets-Style)

**Mechanism:** Match the student's GRU hidden states to a projection of the teacher's hidden states at each timestep. This transfers the teacher's internal representation of market state, not just its outputs.

**Why it fits:** The teacher's hidden state encodes the per-run level and event history. The student's hidden state (256) is smaller than some teachers (384), but matching a projection of the teacher's hidden state can still transfer useful structure. This is especially relevant for the per-run level offset, which is encoded in the hidden state.

**Loss/targets/schedule:** Loss = 0.4 * MSE(student_hidden, teacher_hidden_projected) + 0.4 * MSE(student_output, teacher_output) + 0.2 * MSE(student, label). Teacher hidden projected from 384→256 via a learned linear layer. 6 epochs, lr 5e-5, cosine.

**Signal:** GRU hidden states (intermediate representations).

**Data:** Train split.

**Cheapest falsifier:** Measure hidden state correlation between student and teacher on validation. If correlation is low, the projection is failing.

**Expected gain:** +0.001-0.002.

**Literature:** Romero et al. 2015, "FitNets: Hints for Thin Deep Nets."

---

## 5. Residual-of-Teachers Distillation (Boosting-Style)

**Mechanism:** Instead of distilling the teacher's prediction, distill the teacher's *residual* over the parent. The student learns to predict the correction that the teacher ensemble would apply to the parent's output.

**Why it fits:** The parent is already good (0.666). The teacher ensemble's advantage (+0.003) comes from the residual corrections. By distilling the residual, we focus on what the teachers know that the parent doesn't. This is a 2-stage boosting approach.

**Loss/targets/schedule:** Loss = 0.6 * MSE(student, parent + teacher_residual) + 0.4 * MSE(student, label), where teacher_residual = teacher_ensemble - parent. 6 epochs, lr 5e-5, cosine. Parent is the warm-start checkpoint.

**Signal:** Teacher residual (teacher_ensemble - parent).

**Data:** Train split.

**Cheapest falsifier:** Compare student vs parent on validation. If student ≈ parent, the residual distillation failed (the student didn't learn the correction).

**Expected gain:** +0.002-0.003.

**Literature:** Freund & Schapire 1997, "A Decision-Theoretic Generalization of On-Line Learning and an Application to Boosting."

---

## 6. Rank/Quantile Distillation Within Runs (Unconventional)

**Mechanism:** Instead of distilling exact prediction values, distill the *rank* of each row's prediction within its run. The student learns to predict the relative ordering of rows, which is robust to the per-run level offset problem.

**Why it fits:** The per-run level offset is the dominant error source (94% of residual). By distilling ranks, we remove the level offset from the target and focus on the within-run structure, which is more learnable and transfers better. The t0/t1 difference mode is under-dispersed, suggesting the student struggles with the relative structure.

**Loss/targets/schedule:** Loss = 0.5 * rank_loss(student, teacher) + 0.3 * MSE(student, label) + 0.2 * MSE(student, teacher). Rank loss = 1 - Spearman correlation between student and teacher predictions within each run. 6 epochs, lr 5e-5, cosine.

**Signal:** Rank/quantile of teacher predictions within runs.

**Data:** Train split, grouped by run boundaries.

**Cheapest falsifier:** Compare rank correlation between student and teacher on validation. If rank correlation is high but MSE is low, the level offset is the issue.

**Expected gain:** +0.001-0.002.

**Literature:** Burges et al. 2005, "Learning to Rank using Gradient Descent."

---

## Summary

| Method | Mechanism | Signal | Expected Gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Longer low-LR | Optimization fix | Mean teacher outputs | +0.001-0.002 |
| 2. Per-run level | Target aggregation | Per-run means | +0.001-0.002 |
| 3. Disagreement-weighted | Loss weighting | Teacher variance | +0.001-0.003 |
| 4. Hidden state | Representation transfer | GRU hidden states | +0.001-0.002 |
| 5. Residual-of-teachers | Boosting-style | Teacher - parent | +0.002-0.003 |
| 6. Rank/quantile | Unconventional, robust | Within-run ranks | +0.001-0.002 |

Methods 2, 5, and 6 directly target the per-run level offset (the dominant error source). Method 3 targets the hard class 3 regions. Method 4 transfers internal structure. Method 1 is the cheapest to try (just change the schedule). Method 5 has the highest expected gain because it directly distills the teacher's advantage over the parent.
